Subject: Marketplace listing blocked: need help

Hi Monica,

Quick one — our Nimbus Analytics listing submission on Azure Marketplace is showing a rejection on the review portal with two blocking items: (1) SKU mapping doesn't match the co-sell metering expectations (they expect a per-inference call SKU but our mapping is set to a subscription SKU), and (2) a note about network egress controls / IP egress policy for dedicated customers — marketplace reviewer says we need a short statement or evidence describing how outbound egress is handled for private deployments.

We attached the reviewer screenshot and our current SKU mapping. Can Redwood help escalate the SKU mapping guidance (so the ISV template matches co-sell requirements) and provide a short technical blurb about egress controls we can paste into the marketplace evidence binder?

Samir (cc'd — billing lead) is ready to update pricing if we confirm the required SKU shape. We're trying to avoid a full re-submission cycle if possible. Any chance you can triage or point to the right contact?

Thanks,
Elena Ramos

Thanks for the ping. Quick answers:
- For Azure/AWS co-sell we prefer discrete metered SKUs when the ISV's billing surface is per-inference or per-API-call. That means Samir should publish a metered SKU (units = inference_calls) rather than a subscription SKU. We can provide an example manifest.
- If you can share the target price per inference (even a range), we can patch the SKU metadata in the draft marketplace listing without a full manifest replacement in many cases.

Samir — can you confirm the billing contact info and a rough price target? If you want, I can draft the SKU manifest fields and send over with instructions for the marketplace portal.

ETA: if we get confirmation today we can try to move a patch request through within 48 hours.

—Ben

Elena — attaching a short blurb below that should satisfy the reviewer for egress/isolation guidance. If they request the architecture diagram we have a redacted version ready to go (I can provide it under NDA).

Suggested statement you can paste into the evidence binder:
"Redwood Inference supports private deployment models (VPC and on-prem) where outbound egress from customer-controlled environments is restricted by customer-managed networking (VPC routing, firewall rules, and NAT gateways). For dedicated managed deployments, Redwood's control plane restricts administrative egress to a small set of vendor-hosted endpoints for telemetry and patching; customers may opt into additional isolation controls and bring-your-own-key (BYOK) for KMS to eliminate key egress. We provide an architecture summary and sanitized egress IP range list upon request for marketplace compliance reviews."

Notes:
- If the reviewer wants explicit IP ranges, tell them we will provide a redacted set tied to the environment; we typically don't publish full IP blocks in public docs.
- For SOC2 evidence: we can provide a redacted audit evidence bundle — I'd escalate if they ask for more than the standard marketplace evidence set.

I'll also draft the minimal SKU manifest fields and push to you, Ben — will send a follow up with a sample manifest snippet and a short checklist for Azure.

Vivek Kulkarni
